newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: White S.African bomb suspect in court.
newsitem.headline: White S.African bomb suspect in court.

text.p: A fifth suspect arrested for a Christmas Eve bombing that killed four people in a small South African farming town appeared in court on Monday, and police were reported as saying he would face four murder charges.
Jan van der Westhuizen was caught just inside Namibia at the weekend and was deported swiftly back across the border where he was arrested.
He appeared in court at Worcester, the site of the blasts in the Cape Town area, but his case was postponed until March 6.
National television news quoted police as saying van der Westhuizen would face four murder and four attempted murder charges. Four other men are already under arrest for the attack.

An adult and three children were killed and about 60 people wounded when twin pipe bombs exploded at a supermarket and pharmacy on December 24 in Worcester, 90 km (55 miles) northeast of Cape Town. Most of the casualties were blacks or mixed-race.

An unknown white right-wing group, the Boere Attack Troops, claimed responsibility for the blasts and demanded the release of right-wingers in jail, self-rule for Afrikaners, and a drastic drop in fuel prices.
